item.title: ‘It’s difficult to be positive’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 0-4 defeat
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has admitted that it is difficult to remain positive after his side suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. Pochettino, who was overseeing his first home match as United manager, expressed disappointment with the result but urged his players to remain united and work together to turn around the club’s fortunes. Speaking after the encounter at Old Trafford, the Argentine said United started the match strongly but struggled after conceding the opening goal. “Difficult to be positive. Very disappointed, disappointed at the same time because I feel sorry for the players,” he said. “The players from the beginning, during 15 to 20 minutes, we were very solid, organisation, structure. I think we were controlling the game. The moment we concede the goal, we should not concede this goal.” Callum Wilson scored twice in the first half to put Brentford in control before Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade added two more goals in the closing stages to complete the visitors’ victory. Pochettino admitted that conceding the first goal affected his players’ confidence and made the contest more difficult for them. He insisted that the squad must remain calm despite the difficult situation, adding that he believes the team will improve with time. “The game goes difficult, the intensity, the nerves. This situation, a situation like this, is affecting your confidence, but we need to be united and stay together and keep pushing. “We are going to push to improve and, of course, it is only a matter of time that we are going to improve. We need to stay together, we need to stay calm. That is why we’re here. We have the responsibility to turn this situation into another way,” he added. Asked whether the challenge at Manchester United had been bigger than he initially anticipated, Pochettino said he knew the club was going through difficult circumstances before accepting the job. The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager explained that the team’s busy fixture schedule had also made it difficult to implement his ideas, particularly with three matches played within 10 days. “No, we knew it was going to be bigger. That is why we are here. No change in my view. Only that things need time to change in football more. When the fixtures and schedule is so busy,” he said. He added that the players had remained receptive to his instructions and were making efforts to improve despite the disappointing results. “The reaction of the players when we lost 4-0. They tried and they care. That is the most important thing. We need to feel the pain and increase our standards and try to do anything to be much better.” The defeat extended United’s winless run in the Premier League to 10 matches, their longest such streak since going 11 games without a victory between November 1989 and February 1990. item.title: Netanyahu offers to rotate Israeli premiership with Eisenkot
item.description: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday proposed a rotating premiership with his main rival Gadi Eisenkot, who would go first, with the latter expected to announce the formation of a new government within days. Proposing a unity government in a social media post, Netanyahu said “my responsibility as a leader requires me to set everything aside… and agree that Gadi Eisenkot will serve first as prime minister, while I will serve as alternate prime minister at the beginning of the term”. The offer came one day after Eisenkot vowed to announce the formation of Israel’s next government by the official deadline of December 6, without using the option of a 14-day extension. He is expected to form a coalition with anti-Netanyahu parties, but his centrist Yashar party has also been conducting negotiations with Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud. On Friday, however, Eisenkot accused Likud of stalling coalition talks in a bid to bring about new elections. “Likud… has been unwilling to compromise and, over two weeks, refused to put a single concrete proposal on the table,” Eisenkot said in a statement. His wide-ranging camp has faced divisions over whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, the Arab-majority lists, or form a unity government with Likud. Netanyahu opponents scoffed at his offer of a rotating premiership. Youssef Jabareen, leader of the Arab-majority Joint List, which is expected to support an Eisenkot-led government without joining it, wrote: “The democratic majority has decided: this bloodstained, neglectful government must go. It is time to fulfill the shared will of the entire public, Jews and Arabs alike, and remove Netanyahu this (upcoming) week.” “Netanyahu’s proposal is yet another transparent con by a serial fraudster who has deceived every partner and violated every agreement,” wrote former premier Yair Lapid, co-chair of the centrist Beyachad party. Eisenkot’s Yashar party has so far agreed coalition deals with the left-leaning Democrats and the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party. Together, they have a combined total of 36 lawmakers — far short of the 61 needed for a majority in Israel’s 120-seat parliament. Israeli media reported that Mansour Abbas, the leader of the second Arab-Israeli party, Raam, is expected on Saturday to recognise Hamas as a “terror group” — a move that could pave the way for his party to join a possible Eisenkot-led coalition. But some of Eisenkot’s allies have voiced opposition to relying on the support of the Arab-majority lists, which made unprecedented gains in the election. item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council has accused Vice President Kashim Shettima of abandoning his responsibilities amid Nigerians’ economic hardship to serve as President Bola Tinubu’s campaign attack dog, appearing at political rallies to ridicule former Vice President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The council said rather than explain what the Tinubu administration had done to ease the rising cost of living, Shettima had chosen to attack the opposition. ADC challenged him to account for the soaring prices of food, transportation and electricity. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, on Saturday, the council questioned Shettima’s influence in government and accused him of failing to make a meaningful contribution to decisions affecting the lives of ordinary Nigerians. “Vice President Kashim Shettima has reduced his role in this election to that of Tinubu’s campaign mascot: he appears at rallies to mock Atiku Abubakar, but disappears when Nigerians ask why food, transport and electricity have become so expensive,” it said. The campaign council recalled Shettima’s description of former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo as an “ice cream seller” during the 2023 election campaign, challenging him to show what he had achieved nearly four years into the Tinubu administration. “For the holder of Nigeria’s second-highest office, his contribution to the decisions shaping ordinary lives has been remarkably hard to see,” the statement added. It also questioned Shettima’s standing within the administration, alleging that the President’s wife, his son, Seyi Tinubu, the Chief of Staff and FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, wielded greater influence and commanded more attention than the Vice President. On Shettima’s suggestion that Atiku’s presidential ambition was driven by regional interests, the council insisted that the former Vice President’s campaign had a national appeal, pointing to his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, who hails from the South. “Atiku has taken his Affordable Life message to voters across Nigeria and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, is from the South. Nigerians facing the same hardship across the country do not need Tinubu’s campaign mascot to sort them into regional boxes,” it said. The council also demanded evidence for Shettima’s allegation that Atiku was seeking the presidency to “make money and foment mischief”, describing the accusation as baseless and unbecoming of a holder of the office of Vice President. “Let him produce a shred of evidence or withdraw it. His office does not turn a malicious invention into a fact,” the statement said. item.title: Ex-Lagos deputy gov, Senator Adebule, dies at 56
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State deputy governor and incumbent senator representing Lagos West senatorial district, Dr. Idiat Oluranti Adebule has died barely 24 hours after celebrating her 56th birthday in the state. Adebule, who was seeking re-election for a second term in the Senate, died in the early hours of Saturday. She was pronounced dead by medical experts at a private hospital in Ikeja, G.R.A., Ikeja Local Government Area of the state, where she was admitted after a brief illness. Adebule was said to be battling an undisclosed ailment for several years before she finally succumbed to death on Saturday. She was the deputy to former Governor Akinwunmi Ambode. The Lagos State All Progressives Congress, APC, spokesman, Seye Oladejo, confirmed the death. He described it as “a rude shock.” He prayed the Almighty God forgive her sins and grant his family, friends, and well-wishers the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss. He, however, announced the postponement of the earlier planned senatorial district for the Lagos West senatorial campaign scheduled for next Monday, November 30. It was learned Senator Adebule was already preparing to attend the campaign rally scheduled for Police College, Ikeja, when the tragedy suddenly occurred. item.title: Man Utd thrashed 4-0 by Brentford in Pochettino’s home debut
item.description: Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 at home by Brentford on Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge to leave the 20-time English champions still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone. Callum Wilson struck a first-half double before late goals from Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade sealed Brentford’s first win at Old Trafford for 89 years on Saturday. Pochettino replaced the sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month, tasked with turning around the fortunes of a club in steep decline. However, the Argentine could barely have imagined a worst start after also losing 4-0 away to Liverpool in his first match in charge last weekend. For the first time in 65 years, United have conceded four goals in three consecutive league matches. That shocking defensive record has plunged the Red Devils into a battle for survival. Only Crystal Palace sit below United and Pochettino’s men could slip to the foot of the table if the Eagles beat Hull on Sunday. Pochettino came out fighting after a series of refereeing decisions went against his side against Liverpool and in a controversial 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday. But there was no hiding place for the new boss or his players after their latest embarrassment. Brentford were missing first-choice striker Igor Thiago through suspension, but it mattered little as his deputy Wilson took advantage of United’s disorganised defence. An encouraging start by the home side was quickly forgotten when Wilson lashed home a brilliant finish to open the scoring on 19 minutes. The former Newcastle and West Ham striker then doubled his tally from Dango Ouattara’s pass 13 minutes later. The end of Carrick’s reign was marked by brief flickers of United resistance in comebacks to beat Roma and salvage a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. Youri Tielemans smashed against the crossbar as United pressed for a route back into the game in the second half. But their inability to defend ended any hope of a fightback as Ajer was given way too much space to fire in from a corner. Schade then completed the rout in stoppage time as Brentford climbed to fifth and within one point of the top four. item.title: 2027 : Atiku, Obi relying on regional support to win election, Shettima says
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Vice President Kashim Shettima has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi of relying on regional support in their bid to win the 2027 presidential election. Shettima made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he questioned the opposition candidates’ campaign strategies and their efforts to build support across the country. He said Obi had visited 17 states, including all five states in the South-East and all South-South states except Rivers, but had made limited visits to other regions. According to Shettima, Obi had visited only Kaduna State in the North and Lagos State in the South-West. He also accused the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate of attempting to use religious divisions to advance his political ambition, insisting that elections could not be won through division. “You cannot win election through divisions. We win elections through negotiation, through compromises, through bridge building,” the Vice-President said. Shettima also criticised Atiku’s campaign activities, claiming that the former vice-president had visited only six states and had not travelled to any state in Southern Nigeria. “My brother Atiku Abubakar, he has so far visited six states in the Federation. He has not visited one state in Southern Nigeria. He has concentrated purely in the North,” he said. The Vice-President argued that presidential candidates needed support beyond their traditional political strongholds to secure victory, citing former President Muhammadu Buhari’s eventual success after building an alliance with the South-West. He said Buhari’s support in the North alone had not been enough to secure the presidency until he formed an alliance with the South-West. Shettima expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would defeat the opposition candidates in the 2027 election. item.title: Poor turnout, smooth BVAS operation mark INEC mock polls in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) mock accreditation and voting exercise in selected polling units in Kebbi State on Saturday recorded low voter turnout, although the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines operated without reported malfunctions. The exercise witnessed a predominantly female turnout, with relatively few male voters seen at several polling units visited. At Aliero Housing Estate 006 Primary School polling unit, female voters turned out for accreditation, while only a few male voters were sighted. Security personnel, including officers of the Police, Department of State Services (DSS), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and State Security Service (SCIB), were deployed to provide security during the exercise. INEC ad hoc staff at the polling unit confirmed that the BVAS machines were functioning effectively during voter authentication. A visit to Gwadangaji 001 polling unit also showed a low turnout, with a few female voters presenting themselves for accreditation and no male voters sighted at the time. The voters were seen checking their names on the lists displayed on the walls before proceeding with the exercise. However, at Justice Ibrahim Umar polling unit in the GRA NEPA area, a relatively large number of female voters turned out for the mock exercise. The ad hoc staff confirmed that the two BVAS machines provided for the polling unit were working effectively, adding that no malfunction had been recorded since the exercise commenced at 9 a.m. Meanwhile, an APC stakeholder, Alhaji Abubakar ABK, described the exercise as impressive and peaceful. He attributed the participation of female voters to what he described as the humanitarian interventions of Governor Idris, expressing optimism that voters would turn out in large numbers during the January 2027 general elections. ABK urged voters to maintain the peaceful conduct witnessed during the mock exercise when participating in the main elections in 2027. item.title: INEC Mock Election Scorecard: Low turnouts, poor awareness, BVAS glitches mar exercise
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, organised mocked polls across the country today with mixed results and turnouts. The exercise was to test INEC’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, expecially the technical aspects. However, despite reports of poor numbers, the INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, expressed satisfaction with the conduct of the nationwide mock accreditation exercise. He assured Nigerians of the commission’s readiness to deliver credible elections in 2027. Amupitan, who visited Jos on Saturday to monitor the exercise, inspected polling locations, including Obasanjo Model School in Jos South Local Government Area, where he observed voter accreditation and the performance of electoral technology. Speaking to journalists, the INEC chairman described the turnout and conduct of the exercise as impressive. “You can see yourself that it is very impressive. The turnout is very good,” he said. Uploaded results Meanwhile, about 1,995 results (approximately 12%) of the 17,614 expected, had been uploaded as of 3:09 pm on Saturday in the nationwide INEC mock presidential election. The Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise, which started at 8:30a.m., ended at 2:30pm. However, more than 30 minutes later, the portal puts the “Percentage uploaded” at 11.33 per cent. Its last recorded upload came at 3:09:11 pm from polling unit 32/04/05/005, at press time. Low turnout in Lagos Low turnout of eligible voters marred the mock accreditation exercise conducted in parts of Lagos State, with some voters blaming the commission’s inadequate publicity. Polling agents expressed concern over the poor participation when Vanguard visited some of the designated polling units in Ijegun, Satellite Town and Festac, in the Amuwo-Odofin area of the state. An INEC polling agent at one of the polling units said only about 40 of the 250 registered voters had participated in the exercise as of the time of the visit. …in Katsina, too; poor publicity Also, low voter turnout and inadequate public awareness characterised the mock accreditation exercise conducted by lNEC in Katsina State on Saturday, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vanguard monitoring of the exercise at Star Election Polling Unit, Wakilin Kudu 1, Kofar Gidan Iro Isansi, Rafin Dadi, showed that only a few voters turned out to participate, although some were successfully accredited. The low participation raised concerns about the level of public sensitisation and awareness among eligible voters regarding the importance of the exercise. item.title: 2027: Nigerians determined to vote out APC, says Hashim
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has declared that Nigerians have made up their minds to vote against the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election, accusing the President Bola Tinubu-led administration of worsening the country’s economic and security challenges. Hashim made the declaration on Saturday in Abuja during the flag-off of his presidential campaign, where he promised to build a $4 trillion economy within eight years if elected president. He said economic hardship, rising insecurity, widespread poverty and what he described as the significant collapse of the economy under the APC-led government had strengthened Nigerians’ determination to change the country’s leadership. The Accord presidential candidate cited the reported reach of his recent interview on Symfoni Podcast, which he said was watched by almost 10 million Nigerians and attracted over one million positive reactions, as evidence of growing interest in his presidential ambition. He also alleged that some APC leaders were complicit in the worsening security situation, saying banditry and other forms of criminality had devastated communities across several states. According to him, the 2027 general election would be different, insisting that political victory would not be determined by the ability of parties to fill stadiums during campaigns. He accused the ruling party of already campaigning against itself through its handling of the country’s affairs. “Nigerians will cook APC with cold water,” Hashim declared in Hausa, drawing a loud ovation from the crowd. He further accused the APC of attempting to manipulate the 2027 elections and criticised what he described as exorbitant charges for political campaign billboards in Abuja. However, Hashim ruled out violence as a means of pursuing his presidential ambition, assuring supporters that his campaign would remain peaceful. “We will not resort to violence from our side. We will not incite anybody. I don’t want to lose any of my supporters,” he said. On the economy, the presidential candidate promised that an Accord-led government would restore Nigeria’s economic prosperity, reduce the cost of petroleum products and electricity, and introduce policies that would make energy more affordable. He cited Kuwait and other oil-producing countries as examples of nations where citizens enjoy more affordable energy despite the availability of petroleum resources. Hashim recalled that Nigeria built refineries during the administration of the late Prime Minister, Tafawa Balewa, arguing that the country could achieve significantly better economic results through responsible leadership and prudent management of public resources. item.title: Tinubu’s reforms push Nigeria’s foreign reserves to $54.13bn – City Boy Movement
item.description: The City Boy Movement has hailed the rise in Nigeria’s gross foreign reserves to $54.13 billion, describing the development as evidence of progress under President Bola Tinubu’s economic reform agenda. The group said the reserves had reached their second-highest level on record since 1999, surpassed only by the $62.08 billion peak recorded in September 2008, when the global financial crisis was unfolding. In a statement titled, “Why Tinubu 4+4? Foreign Reserves Edition,” the movement said Nigeria’s foreign reserves had increased significantly under the Tinubu administration, rising from $32.29 billion in May 2023 to $54.13 billion in November 2026. It put the increase at $21.84 billion, representing nearly 68 per cent growth since the President assumed office. According to the group, the latest figures place Nigeria’s foreign reserves above the peak levels recorded in several years, including 2009, 2007, 2013, 2018, 2025, 2019, 2012 and 2014. The movement noted that Nigeria’s reserves peaked at $53.25 billion in 2009, $51.33 billion in 2007, $48.86 billion in 2013 and $47.87 billion in 2018. It added that the $54.13 billion recorded in 2026 represented the highest level since the 2008 global financial crisis. While acknowledging the difficulties associated with the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, the group argued that the latest reserve figures indicated that the policies were beginning to yield positive results. It said the growth in foreign reserves was an important development in assessing the direction of the economy, expressing optimism that the country was moving towards greater economic prosperity. “The significance is in the history. Even though the reforms have been difficult, the numbers are beginning to tell their own story. We are on the way to prosperity,” the statement said. The movement also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for what it described as progress in the management of the country’s external reserves, reaffirming its support for the President. The figures cited by the group were attributed to data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). However, the movement’s assessment comes amid continuing public debate over the impact of the Federal Government’s economic reforms, particularly their effects on inflation, living costs, businesses and household welfare. While higher foreign reserves can strengthen a country’s capacity to meet external obligations and support confidence in its economy, the extent to which the increase translates into improved living conditions remains a key measure of the overall success of the reforms. item.title: [PHOTOS] Moment Voter Makes Frustrating Facial Expressions While Being Captured On INEC’s BVAS
item.description: A voter at polling unit 001 in Barnawa, Kaduna South Local Government Area, captured attention on Saturday, as she made different frustrating facial expressions while being captured on the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) during the INEC’s mock accreditation exercise in Kaduna State. Our correspondent, who monitored the exercise, noted that a voter spent more than five minutes completing the accreditation and voting process due to network challenges affecting the machine. The exercise is expected to simulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Meanwhile, one of the voters at polling unit 002, Narayi Primary School, in Kaduna State, Rebecca Oladipo, has expressed frustration over the absence of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s officials at the mock accreditation on Saturday. Oladipo, who said she arrived at the polling unit for the INEC mock accreditation exercise at 10:30 am, questioned the commission’s preparedness to conduct a credible election in 2027, expressing concern that the mock election, which is expected to test INEC’s operational readiness, appears to be starting on a shaky note. According to her, the delay left those who turned up for the exercise waiting without knowing when the exercise would commence. Rebecca Oladipo “I’m here at Narayi Primary School, one of the wards chosen for the mock exercise. I have been here for the past two hours. INEC is supposed to start the exercise at 8:30. Now we are at around 10:30, and we are yet to see them. “This is really disheartening because a lot of people have been here. Security agencies have been here; even I came to meet them here. One or two voters have been here, and they left. “I’m using this opportunity to say to INEC that we in Narayi ward are not happy because we heard that other wards have started the exercises, so we should not be left behind. “I’m using this opportunity to tell INEC that in the main election, please, please, let it not be like this. It has always been like this in the previous elections. Maybe because Narayi people are good and kind people. They are quiet people. “But please, I hope that everyone knows that the 2027 general election is a critical one. So, we are begging that they should make everything available. “Whatever may make them come late during the 2027 election, they should please avoid it.” The mock exercise, expected to simulate the Presidential election, is expected to open by 8:30 a.m., and accreditation will run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The post [PHOTOS] Moment Voter Makes Frustrating Facial Expressions While Being Captured On INEC’s BVAS appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: PHOTOS: Low Turnout as INEC begins Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) commenced its mock elections in Borno State to test-run voting equipment and logistical readiness ahead of the 2027 general elections. However, the exercise recorded a low voter turnout in some polling units visited by our correspondent due to what many residents described as “a lack of awareness”. The exercise, designed to evaluate the deployment of election personnel and the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) across all 27 local government areas of the state, also faced a slow start in some polling units. Across Jere and Maiduguri Metropolitan Councils security personnel, including police officers and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and Road Safety Officials, were present early at some polling units, INEC officials arrived late. Yul recalls Pete Edochie’s final moments 3 killed, many injured as rival youth groups clash in Cross River At the Bulama Jidda polling unit in Gomari Airport, voting commenced at 8:44 a.m. after officials arrived, slightly behind schedule. However, poll workers and voters at the station confirmed that the BVAS machines functioned efficiently. “There is actually a low turnout, but the use of BVAS is smooth. At some point, we are using it offline, but will upload it when we reach areas with a robust network,” one polling unit officer stated. Interviews with residents across various areas revealed that public awareness of the exercise was generally poor, with many locals unaware that the mock election was taking place. At the Gwange III polling unit, turnout was similarly low. Some prospective voters said they encountered some technical hitches during accreditation, reporting that the BVAS failed to capture their fingerprints and facial features. Speaking on condition of anonymity, an Ad-hoc staff, noted that affected individuals were not issued ballot papers. Instead, their details were compiled for INEC to review and resolve prior to the general elections. At the Government House polling unit (Unit 001, Maisandari Ward), where voter turnout was notably impressive, the process ran without hitches. Abacha Anas, the Electoral Officer for Operations for INEC in the Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, described the exercise as smooth and successful.

item.title: INEC Declares Readiness For 2027, Expresses Satisfaction With Plateau Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Amupitan inspecting the exercise in Jos on Saturday, November 28, 2026. He commended voters for their orderly conduct, expressing delight at seeing an elderly woman turn out for the exercise and successfully undergo accreditation. “You can see yourself that the turnout is very good. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. On the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC was determined to deliver one of the best elections in the country’s history. “For the 2027 general elections, INEC is prepared, and I want to assure all Nigerians that we are going to have one of the best elections. We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” he stated. Addressing concerns over the security situation in the country, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with relevant security agencies to ensure the protection of voters and electoral personnel during the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that INEC recently convened a one-day national security conference where stakeholders deliberated on security challenges and measures to safeguard the electoral process. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, seen addressing staff and voters in Jos on Saturday, NOVEMBER 28, 2026. Amupitan further revealed that the commission had conducted a risk assessment of polling units across the country, with identified locations shared with law enforcement agencies to enable them to strengthen security arrangements ahead of the elections. “We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said. item.title: CHINA DIARIES: Where Students Build the Future
item.description: I must confess, I was not quite prepared for what I saw during my visit to the Qinling Workshop at Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College in China. For someone fascinated by technology and innovation, walking into the institution’s aircraft hangar was an experience in itself. There were aircraft and helicopters, aviation equipment and specialised training facilities. For a moment, it felt less like visiting a school and more like stepping into an aviation engineering centre. But the biggest surprise was yet to come. Beyond the aircraft and helicopters, I encountered something that left an even stronger impression: drones designed, developed and assembled by students. China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents China Diaries: The future of farming These were not simply classroom models or academic projects put together to earn grades. The students were experimenting with different drone technologies, exploring their applications and developing solutions to practical problems. There were different designs and innovations, reflecting the creativity, technical confidence and curiosity of young people who were not waiting until graduation to start making a contribution to society. It was exciting to see. One could immediately imagine the possibilities: drones that could help farmers monitor crops and spray farmlands, support environmental monitoring, conduct aerial surveys, inspect infrastructure and assist emergency response operations. What struck me most was the philosophy behind what I was seeing. Technology was not being taught as an abstract subject. Students were being encouraged to understand problems and develop technological solutions. An institution built around practical skills The Qinling Workshop visit offered an opportunity to appreciate the work of Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College, an institution with a strong focus on aviation, engineering and technical education. Its programmes cover a wide range of disciplines, including aviation manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, aircraft engine technology, drone application technology, general aviation, mechanical engineering, artificial intelligence, computer technology, robotics, automation, electronic information, aviation logistics and automotive technology. Students also study specialised areas such as CNC machining, intelligent manufacturing, aircraft electronic systems, materials engineering, welding technology, surveying and remote sensing, software development, big data, airport operations and civil aviation services. The breadth of these programmes is significant. It shows an understanding that an aviation and manufacturing economy requires much more than pilots and aircraft engineers. It needs technicians, software developers, mechanics, materials specialists, electronics experts, maintenance professionals and people who can design, manufacture and repair equipment.
